title: Make the captain role real
description: Only `admin` unlocks anything today: every route uses RequireRole("admin"), so a captain account signs in and gets a 403. Define two roles with real meaning. Captain: everything a captain does - planning dashboard, availability, selection, fixtures and rescheduling, result entry and match-card import, players and player links, points and standings. Administrator: all of that plus users and invites, sessions and audit log, club settings and feature switches, BHPLTA import configuration, season creation, and backups. Consistent with the club's whole-team ethos, captains see every team; scope filters stay as a focus aid, never a gate. Navigation hides what a role cannot use, and the server enforces it regardless. The unused `player` role is removed from the create-user form (players use link tokens).

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Cross-cutting authorisation change over many routes where a missed route is a security bug.

acceptance_criteria: A captain account can sign in and reach every captain surface for all teams
A captain receives 403 from every administrator-only route, and those links do not appear in captain navigation
Role requirements are declared in one place per route group, with a test that fails if a new /admin/league route is registered without a declared role
Captains can be linked to their player record (users.player_id) so 'My teams' defaults work
Existing administrator accounts keep full access after upgrade
The role names and what each can do are listed in the user guide (Sprint 024)

notes: Do not introduce per-team data isolation - that would contradict the agreed access model.
Push 'notify selected players' and 'remind availability' are captain actions; VAPID reset is administrator-only.

testing_requirements: Table-driven test: every registered route x role -> expected status

context.user_story: As a captain, I want my own login that lets me run my teams without being handed the keys to user management.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
